When edge 1 is absent, node 2 depends on node 1, so removing edge 0 cuts much more of the cell.
Removing the critical residual skip hurts far more than removing a conv on edge 3.
Restoring edge 0 matters most when it is the only route from the input into the intermediate nodes.
With edge 0 absent, edge 1 is the sole input path to the intermediate nodes, so removing it is very damaging.
When edge 5 is missing, edge 4 carries most of the processed signal to the output, so removing it hurts more.

raw:
Each hypothesis below rests on the 100 experiments plus the known structure of NAS-Bench-201. The most common pattern is that an edit's effect gets larger when the parent cell's alternative signal paths are weak or missing.

1. **Edge 3 → skip_connect, when edge 3 is currently none: higher.** Adding the residual where none existed gave large gains (rows 11–16). Replacing an existing conv or pool gave smaller gains (rows 17–18).
2. **Edge 0 → none, when edge 1 is none: lower.** With edge 1 already empty, node 2 can only get input through node 1, so cutting edge 0 disconnects much more (rows 19 and 22 vs 20, 21 and 23).
3. **Edge 3 → none, when edge 3 is skip_connect: lower.** Removing the skip cost 15–56 points (rows 37–40). Removing a conv on that edge cost less (row 41).
4. **Edge 0 → nor_conv_3x3, when edge 1 is none: higher.** Restoring edge 0 matters most when node 2 has no direct input from node 0 (rows 90 and 92 vs 89 and 91).
5. **Edge 1 → none, when edge 0 is none: lower.** With edge 0 empty, edge 1 is the only path from the input into the intermediate nodes (row 79 vs rows 77, 78 and 80).
6. **Edge 4 → none, when edge 5 is none: lower.** With edge 5 empty, the output relies on edges 3 and 4 alone (rows 60–61 vs 62–63).
7. **Edge 0 → skip_connect, when edge 0 is avg_pool_3x3: higher.** Swapping avg-pool out of the first edge gave the biggest gains (row 65 vs rows 64, 66 and 67).
8. **Edge 4 → nor_conv_3x3, when edge 0 is none: lower.** If node 1 receives nothing, a conv on edge 4 has no signal to work with (row 24 vs rows 25–28).
9. **Edge 5 → nor_conv_3x3, when edge 1 is skip_connect: higher.** When the paths into node 2 have no parameters, adding a conv on the last edge helps a lot (row 4 vs the other edge-5 conv edits).
10. **Edge 3 → skip_connect, when edge 4 is none: higher.** If node 1 has no direct route to the output, the input-to-output skip matters most (row 16 vs rows 11, 12 and 15).
